title: Regions, Availability Zones and Local Zones, and what AWS charges to cross them

videos.script: You are about to work on AWS for twenty-six lessons. You will not need an AWS account for any of them. {{lab}} Two programs on your own computer stand in for it. One is the real AWS command line. The other is moto, which answers that command line the way AWS would. {{moto}} This lesson builds that lab, step by step, and shows what to do when a step fails. Then it asks the lab its first questions. Where is AWS? {{map}} AWS is a set of regions, each one a place on the map. Inside each region sit Availability Zones. A zone is a separate failure: its own power, its own network, its own buildings. {{zones}} You spread a system across zones so that it survives losing one. But the zones are not free to cross. {{arrows}} Every arrow between two boxes has a price per gigabyte. Some are free. Some cost a cent. And leaving São Paulo costs almost seven times more than arriving there. {{prices}} Those prices are not guesses. They come from the list AWS publishes, read by a short program you will run yourself. By the end, you can ask your lab where things are, and say what it costs to move between them. {{end}}
